text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today as oil refiners benefited from a week of heightened energy prices driven by Middle East tensions. Despite a small pullback in crude oil prices on Friday (today), the company has climbed 8.9% over two weeks—a period marked by escalating attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure and shipping routes in the Red Sea that have kept crude elevated around $97–$109 per barrel. Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near full tilt, which means the company is converting that higher-priced crude into fuels at a brisk pace.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for refiners: geopolitical risk premiums have spiked energy markets this week, and even though oil prices dipped slightly today, the weekly gains are sharp. Refinery utilization hovering near maximum and relatively tight product inventories (gasoline and diesel storage both at modest levels) suggest strong demand and pricing power for refined products like gasoline and diesel that Marathon sells.
